title: Primary 6 Angles in Composite Figures
seo_title: P6 Angles in Composite Figures Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE)
standard_text: Finding unknown angles, without additional construction of lines, in composite geometric figures involving squares, rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums
meta_desc: Free P6 maths practice: find unknown angles in figures made of triangles, parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums. 100 PSLE-style questions with answers.
key_big: Name the shapes in the figure, then find one angle at a time using an angle fact.
key_sub: Parallelogram ABCD with ∠DAB = 70°: ∠ABC = 180° − 70° = 110°, and ∠BCD = 70° (opposite angles are equal).
body_html:
Find one angle at a time

A composite figure is made of shapes you know: triangles, squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums. Do not draw extra lines. Find the angles you can, one at a time, until you reach the one you want.

Shape or placeAngle fact
Straight lineAngles add up to 180°
At a pointAngles add up to 360°
Two straight lines crossVertically opposite angles are equal
TriangleAngles add up to 180°
Isosceles triangleThe two angles opposite the equal sides are equal
Equilateral triangleEach angle is 60°
Square and rectangleEach angle is 90°
Parallelogram and rhombusOpposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°
TrapeziumThe two angles between the parallel sides add up to 180°

Worked example

Example 1

ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on DC and BE = BC. ∠DAB = 66°. Find ∠EBC.

Step 1: ∠BCD is opposite ∠DAB, so ∠BCD = 66°. Step 2: BE = BC, so triangle BCE is isosceles and ∠BEC = ∠BCE = 66°. Step 3: ∠EBC = 180° − 66° − 66° = 48°.

Answer: 48°

Example 2 (model method)

Two angles of a rhombus next to each other are in the ratio 1 : 4. Find the larger angle.

They add up to 180°. 1 + 4 = 5 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 36°. The larger angle is 4 units = 144°.

Answer: 144°

Write a reason for each step, for example “opposite angles of a parallelogram” or “isosceles triangle”. In the PSLE, method marks are given for clear working.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a triangle is isosceles because it looks like oneUse equal sides only when tick marks or the question say so
Choosing the wrong pair of equal anglesThe equal angles are opposite the equal sides
Using 360° for the angles in a triangleA triangle is 180°. Use 360° for angles at a point or in a 4-sided figure
Saying angles next to each other in a parallelogram are equalOpposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°
Adding the wrong pair in a trapeziumOnly the two angles on a side between the parallel sides add up to 180°
Measuring with a protractorFigures may not be drawn to scale in tests. Calculate

faq.q: What are angles in composite figures in P6 maths?
faq.a: They are questions where you find an unknown angle in a figure made of triangles, squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums. You use angle facts step by step, without drawing extra lines.

faq.q: How do I help my child find unknown angles in PSLE geometry questions?
faq.a: Ask your child to name the shapes in the figure, mark every angle they can find, and write a reason for each step. Most PSLE angle questions need 2 or 3 steps.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with angles in parallelograms?
faq.a: Mixing up which angles are equal. Opposite angles are equal, but angles next to each other add up to 180°.

faq.q: Is this topic in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. The MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus for Primary 6 includes finding unknown angles in composite figures, without additional construction of lines, under Measurement and Geometry.

items.q: AD and BE are straight lines that cross at C. Find ∠DCE.
items.e: ∠ACB = 180° − 58° − 67° = 55°. ∠DCE is vertically opposite ∠ACB, so ∠DCE = 55°.

items.q: In triangle PQR, ∠PQR = 90° and ∠QPR is twice ∠QRP. Find ∠QRP.
items.e: ∠QPR + ∠QRP = 180° − 90° = 90°. ∠QRP is 1 unit and ∠QPR is 2 units: 3 units = 90°, so 1 unit = 30°.
∠ACB = 180° − 63° − 48° = 69°. ∠ACD and ∠ACB are on a straight line: 180° − 69° = 111°.

items.q: The angles in a triangle add up to …
items.e: The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°. Angles at a point add up to 360°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find the unknown angle.
items.e: 57° + 38° = 95°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so 180° − 95° = 85°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. ∠ACB = 180° − 52° − 71° = 57°.

items.q: ∠AOB is a right angle. Find ∠BOC.
items.e: A right angle is 90°. ∠BOC = 90° − 27° = 63°.

items.q: AOB is a straight line. Find ∠COD.
items.e: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 35° + 88° = 123°, and 180° − 123° = 57°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find the unknown angle.
items.e: The unknown angle is vertically opposite 62°. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is 62°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 48° = 132°.
The unknown angle and 74° are on a straight line. 180° − 74° = 106°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 47° and 68°. Find the third angle.
Find ∠ACB.
items.e: ∠ABC is a right angle (90°). ∠ACB = 180° − 90° − 34° = 56°.

items.q: AB and CD are straight lines. Find ∠BOC.
items.e: ∠BOC and ∠AOC are on the straight line AB. ∠BOC = 180° − 38° = 142°.

items.q: ∠p and ∠q are on a straight line. ∠p is 40° more than ∠q. Find ∠p.

items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 105° + 95° = 200°, and 360° − 200° = 160°.

items.q: The two angles marked y are equal. Find ∠y.
items.e: 180° − 50° = 130°. The two equal angles share it: 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

items.q: Three angles at a point are 140°, 95° and ∠x. Find ∠x.
items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 140° + 95° = 235°, and 360° − 235° = 125°.

items.q: Arjun says ∠x = 242°, because the angles in a triangle add up to 360°. Is he right?
items.e: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°, not 360°. ∠x = 180° − 70° − 48° = 62°.
Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°, and 240° ÷ 3 = 80°.

items.q: In triangle PQR, PQ = QR. Find ∠PQR.
In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Kavya says ∠BAC = ∠ABC. Is she right?
items.e: The equal angles are opposite the equal sides. AB and AC are equal, so ∠ACB (opposite AB) = ∠ABC (opposite AC).

items.q: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. BCD is a straight line. Find ∠BAC.
Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = AC. ∠ABC = 72°. Find ∠BAC.
BDC is a straight line and AD = DC. Find ∠ACD.
In triangle ABC, AB = BC. Find ∠BAC.
items.e: AB = BC, so the equal angles are ∠BAC and ∠BCA (opposite the equal sides), not ∠ABC. 180° − 30° = 150°, and 150° ÷ 2 = 75°.

items.q: ABC and CED are equilateral triangles. BCE is a straight line. Find ∠ACD.
items.e: ∠ACB = 60° and ∠DCE = 60°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: ∠ACD = 180° − 60° − 60° = 60°.

items.q: In triangle XYZ, XY = XZ and ∠YXZ = 48°. Find ∠XYZ.
In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Find ∠ABC.
ABCD is a square and DCE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: ∠ADC = 90° (square) and ∠CDE = 60° (equilateral triangle). ∠ADE = 90° + 60° = 150°.

items.q: ABC is an equilateral triangle and BCD is a straight line. Find ∠ACD.
items.e: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so ∠ACB = 60°. ∠ACD = 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.q: In triangle ABC, CA = CB. Find ∠x.
items.e: The two base angles are equal. 180° − 80° = 100°, and 100° ÷ 2 = 50°.

items.q: In triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 90° and AB = BC. Find ∠BAC.
items.e: ∠BAC + ∠BCA = 180° − 90° = 90°. They are equal, so ∠BAC = 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.
No sides are marked equal, so do not assume the triangle is isosceles. ∠ACB = 180° − 70° − 44° = 66°.

items.q: ABC is an equilateral triangle. D is on BC. Find ∠ADC.
items.e: ∠ABD = 60°. In triangle ABD, ∠ADB = 180° − 60° − 45° = 75°. BDC is a straight line, so ∠ADC = 180° − 75° = 105°.

items.q: ABCD is a square and ABE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠EBC.
items.e: ∠ABC = 90° (square) and ∠ABE = 60° (equilateral triangle). ∠EBC = 90° − 60° = 30°.

items.q: An isosceles triangle has an angle of 110°. Find the other two angles.
items.e: Two angles of 110° would be more than 180°, so 110° is the angle between the equal sides. 180° − 110° = 70°, and 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

items.q: D is on BC and AD = BD. Find ∠ADC.
An isosceles triangle has an angle of 50°. What could the other two angles be?
items.e: If 50° is one of the two equal angles: 180° − 50° − 50° = 80°. If 50° is the other angle: (180° − 50°) ÷ 2 = 65°. Both are possible.
In a parallelogram, angles next to each other add up to 180°. ∠ABC = 180° − 65° = 115°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on DC. Find ∠EBC.
items.e: ∠ABC is opposite ∠ADC, so ∠ABC = 70°. ∠EBC = 70° − 45° = 25°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠ABD.
items.e: AB = AD, so triangle ABD is isosceles and ∠ABD = ∠ADB. 180° − 64° = 116°, and 116° ÷ 2 = 58°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠BAC.
items.e: AB = BC, so triangle ABC is isosceles and ∠BAC = ∠BCA. 180° − 100° = 80°, and 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

items.q: In parallelogram WXYZ, ∠WXY is 30° more than ∠XYZ. Find ∠WXY.
ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram with 4 equal sides. ∠ABC and ∠BCD are next to each other: 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠x.
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°: x + 2x = 3x = 180°. So x = 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

items.q: In parallelogram PQRS, ∠PQR = 74°. Find ∠QRS.
items.e: ∠PQR and ∠QRS are next to each other, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 74° = 106°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠DAC.
items.e: ∠DAB = 180° − 112° = 68° (angles next to each other). ∠DAC = 68° − 38° = 30°.

items.q: One angle of a rhombus is 48°. Find the other three angles.
items.e: The opposite angle is also 48°. Each angle next to it is 180° − 48° = 132°. Check: 48° + 132° + 48° + 132° = 360°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram and DCE is a straight line. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: ∠BCD = 180° − 58° = 122° (straight line). ∠ABC and ∠BCD are next to each other: 180° − 122° = 58°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠ABC.
ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠y.
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°: 3y + 2y = 5y = 180°. So y = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Which two angles are always equal?
items.e: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal: ∠DAB = ∠BCD and ∠ABC = ∠CDA. Angles next to each other add up to 180°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram and ABE is a straight line. Find ∠ADC.
items.e: ∠ABC = 180° − 70° = 110° (straight line). ∠ADC is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠ADC = 110°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠ABD.
items.e: In triangle ABD: ∠ABD = 180° − 105° − 40° = 35°.
∠ADC is opposite ∠ABC. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠ADC = 128°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: ∠BCD is opposite ∠DAB. Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so ∠BCD = 72°.

items.q: What do the four angles of a parallelogram add up to?
items.e: A parallelogram is a 4-sided figure. Its two pairs of angles next to each other each add up to 180°: 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. Zhi Hao says ∠ABC = 58°, because opposite angles are equal. Is he right?
items.e: ∠ABC is next to ∠DAB, not opposite it. Angles next to each other add up to 180°: 180° − 58° = 122°. The angle opposite ∠DAB is ∠BCD.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC and ∠ADC = 90°. Find ∠ACD.
ABCD is a trapezium with AD // BC. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: Here the parallel sides are AD and BC. ∠BAD and ∠ABC are on side AB, between them, so they add up to 180°. ∠ABC = 180° − 118° = 62°.
∠BCD pairs with ∠ABC (the two angles on side BC): 180° − 65° = 115°. ∠DAB pairs with ∠ADC, not with ∠BCD.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: ∠ABC and ∠BCD are between the parallel sides, so they add up to 180°. ∠BCD = 180° − 62° = 118°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠DAC.
items.e: ∠DAB = 180° − 105° = 75° (angles between the parallel sides). ∠DAC = 75° − 40° = 35°.

items.q: In trapezium PQRS, PQ // SR and ∠QPS = 64°. Find ∠PSR.
items.e: ∠QPS and ∠PSR are on side PS, between the parallel sides. They add up to 180°: 180° − 64° = 116°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: ∠ABC and ∠BCD are between the parallel sides: ∠BCD = 180° − 58° = 122°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Which two angles must add up to 180°?
items.e: The two angles on a side that joins the parallel sides add up to 180°: ∠DAB + ∠ADC and ∠ABC + ∠BCD.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. AD and BC are made longer to meet at E. Find ∠EDC.
items.e: ∠ADC = 180° − 70° = 110° (angles between the parallel sides). ADE is a straight line, so ∠EDC = 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.q: In trapezium KLMN, KL // NM. ∠KLM is 3 times ∠LMN. Find ∠LMN.
items.e: ∠KLM + ∠LMN = 180°. ∠LMN is 1 unit and ∠KLM is 3 units: 4 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 45°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. ABE is a straight line. Find ∠BCD.
items.e: ∠ABC = 180° − 72° = 108° (straight line). ∠ABC and ∠BCD are between the parallel sides: 180° − 108° = 72°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠DBC.
items.e: ∠ABC = 180° − 115° = 65° (angles between the parallel sides). ∠DBC = 65° − 35° = 30°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC and AD = DC. Find ∠CAB.
PQRS is a trapezium with PS // QR. Find ∠QRS.
items.e: ∠PSR and ∠QRS are on side RS, between the parallel sides PS and QR. ∠QRS = 180° − 75° = 105°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠x.
ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠ACB.
items.e: In triangle ABC: ∠ACB = 180° − 110° − 30° = 40°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Ahmad says ∠ABC = 112°, because 180° − 68° = 112°. Is he right?
items.e: ∠DAB pairs with ∠ADC (both on side AD). So ∠ADC = 180° − 68° = 112°. ∠ABC cannot be found from ∠DAB alone.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. Find ∠ADC.
items.e: ∠DAB and ∠ADC are between the parallel sides, so they add up to 180°. ∠ADC = 180° − 70° = 110°.

items.q: In trapezium ABCD, AB // DC, ∠DAB = 56° and ∠BCD = 104°. Find ∠ADC + ∠ABC.
ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. E is on AB. Find ∠EDC.
items.e: ∠ADC = 180° − 64° = 116° (angles between the parallel sides). ∠EDC = 116° − 50° = 66°.

items.q: Three angles at a point, ∠p, ∠q and ∠r, are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find ∠r.
items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units = 360°, so 1 unit = 40°. ∠r = 4 units = 160°.

items.q: ABC is an equilateral triangle and CA = CD. Find ∠BAD.
ABCD is a square and ABE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠AEC.
items.e: ∠EBC = 90° − 60° = 30°. BE = BA = BC, so triangle EBC is isosceles: ∠BEC = (180° − 30°) ÷ 2 = 75°. ∠AEC = ∠AEB + ∠BEC = 60° + 75° = 135°.

items.q: ABCD is a square and DCE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠BAE.
In the figure, AB = AC and BD = BC. D is on AC. Find ∠DBC.
ABCD is a parallelogram and DCE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: ∠ADC = 180° − 75° = 105° (angles next to each other). ∠CDE = 60°. ∠ADE = 105° + 60° = 165°.

items.q: BCD is a straight line. AB = AC and CE = DE. Find ∠ACE.
ABCD is a rectangle. E is on DC and DE = DA. Find ∠EBC.
items.e: DE = DA and ∠ADE = 90°, so ∠DEA = 45°. On the straight line DC: ∠CEB = 180° − 45° − 75° = 60°. In triangle EBC: ∠EBC = 180° − 90° − 60° = 30°.

items.q: Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = AC. ∠ABC is twice ∠BAC. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: ∠ACB = ∠ABC, so both are 2 units. 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 units = 180°. 1 unit = 36°, so ∠ABC = 72°.

items.q: In triangle ABC, ∠ABC is 3 times ∠BAC. ∠ACB is 20° more than ∠BAC. Find ∠ABC.
items.e: 5 units + 20° = 180°. 5 units = 160°, so 1 unit = 32°. ∠ABC = 3 units = 96°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus and BCE is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: ∠ABE = 70° + 60° = 130°. AB = BC = BE, so triangle ABE is isosceles: ∠BAE = (180° − 130°) ÷ 2 = 25°.

items.q: ABCD is a rhombus. Find ∠ACD.
items.e: ∠ADC is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠ADC = 116°. CD = DA, so triangle ACD is isosceles: ∠ACD = (180° − 116°) ÷ 2 = 32°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. E is on DC and AD = AE. Find ∠DAE.
items.e: ∠ADC is opposite ∠ABC, so ∠ADC = 68°. AD = AE, so ∠AED = 68°. ∠DAE = 180° − 68° − 68° = 44°.

items.q: Two angles next to each other in a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 7. Find the smaller angle.
items.e: Angles next to each other add up to 180°. 2 + 7 = 9 units. 9 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 20°. The smaller angle is 2 units = 40°.

items.q: AD and BE are straight lines that cross at C. Find ∠CED.
items.e: ∠ACB = 180° − 58° − 67° = 55°. ∠DCE is vertically opposite, so ∠DCE = 55°. ∠CED = 180° − 55° − 70° = 55°.

items.q: ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. E is on AB and EBCD is a parallelogram. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: In parallelogram EBCD, ∠DEB = 180° − 70° = 110°. AEB is a straight line, so ∠AED = 180° − 110° = 70°. In triangle ADE: ∠ADE = 180° − 48° − 70° = 62°.

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram and AB = BD. Find ∠DBC.
ABCD is a square. E is on BC. Find ∠ADE.
ABCD is a trapezium with AB // DC. E is on AB, DA = DE and ∠ADC = 112°. Find ∠EDC.
